issues.body: resolve_trust_surface_paths now deliberately subtracts any exact DEFAULT_TRUST_SURFACE_PATHS entry named by policy. For example, denying containers/ makes a containers/worker-model.Dockerfile change disappear from both review-outcome classification and ready_and_arm's live SHA-bound audit derivation. Keeping at least one unrelated surface does not fail closed for the removed path: a change wholly inside the denied tree receives no trust-surface audit evidence. The reviewer rules explicitly require rejection of changes that delete, relax, or skip the arm-side trust_surface_paths_touched classifier or weaken its audit trail.
issues.fix_hint: Do not make mandatory defaults subtractable. Keep policy security_paths additive and the DEFAULT_TRUST_SURFACE_PATHS union unconditional. If a target needs a narrower concept, represent target applicability without removing the mandatory arm-side audit evidence, and obtain an explicit revision to the standing trust rule before implementing any subtraction.
issues.title: Mandatory arm-side trust surfaces can now be removed

issues.body: The new helper tests call resolve_trust_surface_paths directly, and policy-resolve tests only serialization. Nothing asserts that both live workflow sites pass --deny-surface-path, that the flag is exact and adjacent to each decoded value, or that main forwards args.deny_surface_path to both review_outcome and ready_and_arm. Deleting either new while-loop, renaming its flag, or dropping either production call-site argument would leave the added tests green. This is precisely the YAML/call-site seam where a control can become inert.
issues.fix_hint: Add offline structural tests that parse review-fix.yml and assert exact --deny-surface-path token membership at both the review-outcome and ready-and-arm sites, plus CLI/call-site tests that invoke main with a deny value and prove it reaches each consumer. Use an expected literal independent of the production constant, and include a mutation check showing each dropped site turns a named test red.
issues.title: The trust-sensitive YAML and CLI wiring has no non-vacuous seam test

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

Request changes. This introduces an explicit path for repository policy to remove entries from the arm-side mandatory trust-surface classifier. That weakens the audit trail protecting changes under those paths, contrary to the standing never-weaken rule; exact matching and a non-empty remainder do not preserve coverage of the removed surface. In addition, the new trust-sensitive value is tested only inside the Python helpers: there is no structural test of either workflow call site or of the CLI-to-function call site, so dropping or misspelling the new flag at the YAML seam would leave the full self-test suite green while silently changing the feature's behavior.
